title: Measuring the internal resistance of a cell
body: A student connects a high-resistance voltmeter across the terminals of a dry cell. With nothing else connected, the voltmeter reads 1.50 V. She then connects a 2.0 ohm resistor across the terminals, and the voltmeter now reads 1.20 V. She notes that the cell has a fixed emf and a fixed internal resistance, and that the voltmeter draws a negligible current, so the first reading can be taken as the emf of the cell. She wants to use these two readings to find the internal resistance of the cell and to predict how the cell would behave with other external loads.
